_: THE WORKED-EXAMPLE ATLAS. Four INDEPENDENT design axes. Composition describes the spatial relationship of content that is CURRENTLY VISIBLE; it does not decide whether several pieces of content are visible at the same time. That is disclosure, and it is a separate authored decision. Scroll behaviour is a third. This is a non-shipping reference atlas; the implementation is frozen.
axes: content type       example · explanation · comparison · visual · practice          author
composition        the spatial relationship of what is visible now                 authored
disclosure         continuous · tabs · staged views                                authored
media subdesign    portrait / balanced / landscape / wide figure treatment         figure's own geometry
responsive state   the template's prescribed wide/narrow arrangement               surface width
scroll policy      page · local-y · local-x · persistent-pane                      authored
theHardRule: TABS ARE AUTHORED PEDAGOGICAL STRUCTURE. They may never be introduced or removed because of viewport size, content height, occupancy, or any layout heuristic. `This got tall, so I will hide half of it in tabs` is resolver behaviour and is forbidden. The build asserts that the tab structure — count, labels, nesting — is character-identical at every width.

compositions._: The spatial relationship of currently visible content. Rigid horizontally, fluid vertically.

single.flow.wide: one column at the flow measure: title · QUESTION · rule · WORKED SOLUTION · ANSWER

comparison.sharedVisual.wide: cases across, then the visual and its interpretation

visual.interpretation.authoredAs: visual.interpretation — the author names the composition; the FIGURE'S media-geometry class resolves the suffix. This is the one automatic classification the atlas permits, and it is a property of the figure, never of the prose beside it.

subdesigns.side: FIGURE │ INTERPRETATION — portrait or balanced figure
subdesigns.down: the figure at the atlas's wide width, interpretation beneath — landscape or wide figure

collections._: Several instances of one kind of thing. A collection is not a composition: it says how many are visible, not how one is arranged.

collection.repeat.purpose: every item visible, one after another — when seeing the sequence together is the point
collection.repeat.note: This is what `sequence.flow` was. The count is nowhere in the geometry.

collection.tabs.purpose: one item visible at a time — when showing all of them would make a long repetitive page
collection.tabs.note: Often preferable to collection.repeat on a Notes or Worked Examples page. Both remain available; the author chooses.

presentations._: Staged alternative views of ONE idea. Not a collection of different things — the same thing, seen another way.

presentation.tabs.purpose: authored alternative representations, e.g. 1 Workings · 2 Graph check
presentation.tabs.note: This is what `visualCheck` was. It is not responsive behaviour; it is a pedagogical relationship — solve it one way, then inspect the same idea visually.

presentation.stepper.purpose: an ordered walk through stages of one derivation
presentation.stepper.status: named for completeness; not exercised in this pass

tabPatterns.exampleTabs: several examples of the same skill — Negative value · Fraction · Decimal
tabPatterns.representationTabs: the same idea seen another way — 1 Workings · 2 Graph check
tabPatterns.subtopicTabs: different subtopics, each free to contain a different approved composition — Substitution · Solving for x · Symmetry

scroll._: Three genuinely different things, which the program must not confuse.

scroll.page.meaning: normal and desirable. Notes, examples, derivations and explanations are as tall as they need to be.
scroll.page.rule: Ordinary teaching content ALWAYS uses page scroll. It is never compressed to fit a viewport.

scroll.local-y.rule: PERMITTED ONLY inside a persistent-pane workspace. Ordinary prose and worked solutions must never sit in a local vertical scroll container — that makes the lesson a dashboard rather than courseware.

scroll.local-x.meaning: a local escape hatch for indivisible material
scroll.local-x.rule: A very long equation or table scrolls horizontally rather than shrinking typography or destroying its composition.

scroll.persistent-pane.meaning: one pane scrolls while another stays visible — the Practice workbook shape
scroll.persistent-pane.rule: The only context in which local-y is legitimate.
scroll.persistent-pane.narrow: the bound is given up entirely and the page scrolls — a bounded scroller inside a phone-width page is two scrollbars fighting

assembly._: How the axes compose. The Symmetry topic in the reference page is:
assembly.note: Far more generalisable than inventing a bespoke layout per page.
assembly.divergence: The tree above names visual.interpretation.down for the Symmetry topic's Visual explanation. The atlas renders it .side, because the figure that matches those two cases (y = x^2 with the line y = 9) is BALANCED, and the subdesign is the figure's to decide. Hard-coding .down in an authored tree would be exactly the confusion the axis separation exists to prevent. visual.interpretation.down is exercised at images 10 and 12, where the figure really is wide.

measures._: Design-system values. They never appear in lesson JSON. paneH/paneMinH bound the ONE pane the atlas permits to scroll locally; in the app that height comes from the workspace viewport, never from how long the lesson is.

figureClasses._: Media geometry, from the authored domain's aspect at equal unit scale. A DESIGN INPUT, never a size.

invariants.identity: A composition, a collection and a presentation are all authored and never inferred. The build asserts `data-tpl` and the full tab structure are identical at every width and for every adversarial payload.
invariants.height: height:auto. The page scrolls. Nothing is shrunk, compressed or recomposed to avoid it, and page height is never an optimisation target.
invariants.measure: Every prose region has a controlled measure. Unused page width is reading margin and is correct.
invariants.figures: A figure is sized from its own requirements. Surrounding prose never determines its width.
